title: Archon — Reliability, Security, and Operations
purpose: Understand failure containment, delegation, MCP, observability, and local operations.
limitations: This is derivative learning material, not canonical implementation evidence.
Local deterministic and Docker evidence does not establish production SLOs, public deployment, or resistance to host compromise.
One bounded verifier child and governed MCP are not a distributed autonomous agent network.

concepts.label: Admission and Rate Limits
concepts.summary: Shared Redis windows bound request admission and fail closed when the configured shared limiter is unavailable.

teaching.definition: Admission control decides whether an authenticated action enters expensive runtime work before provider or tool resources are consumed.
teaching.responsibility: Apply atomic shared limits and return a bounded retry-after signal when capacity is exceeded.
controls: Redis failure does not silently downgrade to process-local state
teaching.failure_behavior: Exceeded limits reject early; configured Redis errors fail rather than creating inconsistent per-process enforcement.
teaching.why_it_matters: Reliability starts before execution by bounding demand and avoiding hidden multi-process inconsistencies.

concepts.boundary: Local limiter mode is process-local and no public traffic fairness or capacity SLO is claimed.
concepts.narration: Admission control protects expensive work before it starts. The verified target uses Redis-backed atomic windows; if that shared dependency fails, Archon does not silently replace it with weaker per-process enforcement.
concepts.scenario: Redis-backed limiting is configured, but Redis becomes unavailable.
options: Fail the shared limiter path explicitly
Send the request directly to the provider
concepts.scenario_explanation: Silent fallback would create inconsistent enforcement across processes.

concepts.label: Deadlines and Cancellation
concepts.summary: Absolute deadlines and cancellation paths bound waits and preserve truthful terminal state.

teaching.definition: A deadline is a finite wall-clock budget propagated across provider, persistence, approval, tool, and cleanup waits; cancellation is a distinct external stop signal.
teaching.responsibility: Stop work at the budget boundary, perform one shielded terminal write, and re-raise cancellation when required.
controls: Cleanup cannot start competing terminal sequences
teaching.failure_behavior: If terminal persistence cannot finish within its own bound, the state is logged as indeterminate rather than fabricated.
teaching.why_it_matters: An agent that can wait forever or hide interrupted work is neither bounded nor auditable.

concepts.boundary: In-process cancellation cannot forcibly kill arbitrary cancellation-resistant code; harder isolation belongs to the sandbox boundary.
concepts.narration: Deadlines bound the whole operation, while cancellation records that work was stopped. Archon uses one bounded terminal path; a timeout or incomplete cleanup never becomes a PASS.
concepts.scenario: A provider call exceeds the absolute run deadline after partial progress.
concepts.scenario_explanation: The run must terminate truthfully at the deadline.

concepts.label: Circuit Breaker and Fallback
concepts.summary: A lock-protected breaker stops repeated unhealthy calls; typed fallback preserves the complete required contract or fails.

teaching.definition: The circuit breaker is an app-scoped state machine that opens after classified failures, rejects while open, and admits one half-open recovery probe.
teaching.responsibility: Prevent repeated calls to an unhealthy dependency and select fallback only when one candidate satisfies the whole request contract.
controls: No silent downgrade from tools, images, or structured output to plain text
teaching.failure_behavior: Probe failure or cancellation reopens the breaker; no eligible provider yields a typed error rather than outage prose.
teaching.why_it_matters: Availability measures must not quietly remove the capabilities or safety contract the caller required.

concepts.boundary: Breaker state is process-local; deterministic fallback tests do not prove live cross-provider parity.
concepts.narration: The circuit breaker stops hammering an unhealthy provider and admits one recovery probe. Fallback is allowed only when a candidate preserves the entire typed contract.
concepts.scenario: The primary fails, but the fallback cannot support required tool calls.
options: Raise typed exhaustion because the contract cannot be preserved
concepts.scenario_explanation: Fallback must preserve complete requirements rather than degrade silently.

concepts.label: Durable Idempotency
concepts.summary: Durable reservations and first-writer rules reduce duplicate effects and budget charges under contention.

teaching.definition: Idempotency is the contract that repeated delivery of the same logical operation does not create uncontrolled duplicate durable effects.
teaching.responsibility: Linearize reservations and reconcile one winning durable outcome before or around effect dispatch.
teaching.failure_behavior: Ambiguous downstream outcomes remain indeterminate and require reconciliation; they are not blindly retried as if no effect occurred.
teaching.why_it_matters: Network and process failures create duplicates precisely when a side effect is hardest to inspect.

concepts.boundary: A durable reservation is not universal exactly-once semantics across arbitrary external services.
concepts.narration: Idempotency gives repeated delivery a stable identity and one durable reservation winner. It reduces duplicate effects, but external exactly-once execution still requires downstream reconciliation.
concepts.scenario: A timeout occurs after an external service may have accepted a write.
options: Record ambiguity and reconcile by idempotency identity
concepts.scenario_explanation: The outcome is indeterminate until reconciled.

concepts.label: Bounded Verifier Child
concepts.summary: One signed evidence-only child has no tools, strict output, finite budgets, and durable parent-child lineage.

teaching.definition: Bounded delegation assigns one finite evidence-review task to a child run under a signed scope envelope.
receives: One-time nonce and strict verdict schema
teaching.responsibility: Ask a model for a narrow support judgment while deterministic code validates identity, freshness, budget, content hashes, and output shape.
controls: Replay and content mutation are rejected
teaching.failure_behavior: Malformed, stale, replayed, failed, timed-out, or over-budget child output supports no claim.
teaching.why_it_matters: A second model adds another opinion, not authority; narrow input and deterministic validation keep its blast radius measurable.

concepts.boundary: The verdict remains model-generated and can be wrong; this is one specialist, not a swarm or remote multi-node network.
concepts.narration: Delegation is intentionally narrow: one signed, evidence-only, no-tools verifier child. Code validates the envelope and verdict shape; the model judgment remains fallible.
concepts.scenario: A child returns persuasive prose instead of the strict verdict schema.
options: Fail closed and support no claim
concepts.scenario_explanation: Output outside the declared contract has no authority.

concepts.label: Governed MCP
concepts.summary: Allowlisted stdio and bounded HTTP capabilities remain disabled by default and pass normal schema, policy, approval, and TOCTOU checks.

teaching.definition: Governed MCP is the capability path that discovers external tool metadata without equating portability or discovery with trust.
teaching.responsibility: Discover, store, enable, materialize, authorize, and invoke MCP tools through the same runtime controls as native tools.
controls: Profile and schema hash rechecked immediately before execution
teaching.failure_behavior: Stale profile, schema mismatch, disabled state, unhealthy transport, policy denial, or timeout prevents invocation.
teaching.why_it_matters: A protocol standardizes communication but cannot decide whether a capability should be visible or allowed.

concepts.boundary: No public marketplace, arbitrary package execution, generic OAuth platform, or multi-region gateway is claimed.
concepts.narration: MCP standardizes discovery and calls, not trust. Archon keeps inventory scoped and disabled by default, then rechecks profile, schema, policy, approval, and health before invocation.
concepts.scenario: An MCP server changes a tool schema after approval but before execution.
concepts.scenario_explanation: Execution-time schema revalidation protects the approved contract.

concepts.label: Logs, Metrics, and Traces
concepts.summary: Safe operational signals and durable events provide complementary views without exposing raw secrets or hidden reasoning.

teaching.definition: Observability correlates structured logs, metrics, OTLP spans, SSE progress, and Run Ledger records around a scoped request.
receives: Latency, usage, status, and dependency signals
teaching.responsibility: Make system behavior diagnosable while keeping raw prompts, credentials, tool payloads, and chain-of-thought outside telemetry.
produces: Exported traces and inspectable run events
controls: Allowlists and hashes for sensitive event fields
teaching.failure_behavior: Collector existence without active export is not readiness; telemetry loss does not rewrite durable run outcomes.
teaching.why_it_matters: Different signals answer different questions, and correlation allows them to be investigated without conflating them.

concepts.boundary: The local Collector fans out to allowlisted destinations. Jaeger is loopback-only; Logfire is external. Production retention, alerts, sampling, and SLOs are not proved.
concepts.narration: Logs, metrics, traces, SSE, and the Run Ledger are complementary. Archon emits once to the Collector, which can fan out to Jaeger and Logfire. Content stays off by default; the opt-in exports only redacted and bounded user and assistant text.
concepts.scenario: The OTEL collector process is up, but the backend exporter is inactive.
options: Fail readiness for configured inactive telemetry
concepts.scenario_explanation: Readiness must reflect active export, not object or process existence.

concepts.label: Health and Readiness
concepts.summary: Liveness answers whether the process responds; readiness verifies dependencies and configured capabilities needed for service.

teaching.definition: Health and readiness are separate operational contracts: liveness checks process responsiveness, while readiness checks critical dependency availability and configuration.
teaching.responsibility: Expose whether the service should receive traffic without turning partial dependency failure into a green signal.
controls: Redis is required in the verified target
Mock and live embedding capability remain distinguishable
teaching.failure_behavior: A failed dependency makes readiness fail while the process may remain live for diagnosis.
teaching.why_it_matters: Routing traffic to a live but unusable process produces harder failures and misleading operational claims.

concepts.boundary: A successful readiness probe is a point-in-time local observation, not a production availability guarantee.
concepts.narration: Health says the process responds. Readiness asks whether PostgreSQL, Redis, embedding capability, and telemetry configuration can support the selected target. They must not be collapsed.
concepts.scenario: The API process responds, but PostgreSQL is unavailable.
options: Liveness may pass while readiness fails
concepts.scenario_explanation: The process can be alive while unable to serve correctly.

concepts.label: Base Local Target and Optional Jaeger
concepts.summary: The managed target retains seven base services; an explicitly selected Jaeger profile adds an eighth loopback-only trace UI.

teaching.definition: The local target is a reproducible seven-container base topology with optional profiles, operated through a wrapper that retains exact project and protected configuration pointers.
receives: Managed start, status, logs, and stop commands
teaching.responsibility: Build, migrate, start, verify, retain, inspect, and explicitly stop one known local topology plus selected profiles.
produces: Seven base services and selected profiles
controls: Application and optional Jaeger UI bind only to loopback
Protected env is never reconstructed with dummy secrets
teaching.failure_behavior: Missing retained configuration or failed health preserves diagnostic state rather than inventing credentials or destroying data automatically.
teaching.why_it_matters: A canonical operational interface prevents ad hoc Compose commands from bypassing security and evidence assumptions.

concepts.boundary: Local Compose is not public, cloud, Kubernetes, multi-host, or production operation.
concepts.narration: The managed local target retains seven base services. Optional Jaeger adds an eighth service and a separate loopback-only UI. The wrapper preserves exact runtime context without exposing or fabricating secrets.
concepts.scenario: A retained stack has a missing protected env file.
options: Stop and diagnose from managed metadata
concepts.scenario_explanation: The runbook forbids fabricated credentials and destructive guessing.

concepts.label: Backup and Recovery
concepts.summary: Checksummed PostgreSQL backup and clean restore preserve selected evidence and measure one local restore observation.

teaching.definition: Recovery is the controlled path from a protected custom-format PostgreSQL dump through checksum validation into a clean target and verified application readiness.
receives: Dump, checksum, metadata, and clean destination
teaching.responsibility: Back up durable state atomically, refuse unsafe targets, restore, migrate, authenticate, and compare selected records and hashes.
produces: Measured record difference and restore-to-ready observation
teaching.failure_behavior: Checksum mismatch or non-empty target blocks restore; missing memory key continuity can leave ciphertext unreadable.
teaching.why_it_matters: Backup existence matters only when a clean restore proves the evidence can be recovered.

concepts.boundary: No scheduled retention, PITR, remote encrypted store, cloud failover, or organization-approved RTO/RPO is claimed.
concepts.narration: Recovery verifies more than dump creation: checksum, clean target, restore, migrations, authentication, and exact selected records. One measured Mac run remains an observation, not a business SLO.
concepts.scenario: A restore target already contains Archon user tables.
options: Refuse and create a clean target unless destruction is explicitly approved
concepts.scenario_explanation: Clean-target refusal prevents accidental destructive replacement.
